Power Flow I

Buxin She

Lecture outline
1 System components and their voltage, current, and power quantities.
2 Physical equations: branch currents, complex power, and bus balance.
3 Exercise: write the physical equations for a given network.

Submit the physical relations. No voltage solution or numerical calculation is required.

Reference: branch and bus currents
For each series branch (𝑖, 𝑘) ∈ {(1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 3)}:
𝐼𝑖𝑘 = 𝑦 𝑖𝑘(𝑉𝑖 − 𝑉𝑘), 𝐼 𝑘𝑖 = 𝑦 𝑖𝑘(𝑉𝑘 − 𝑉𝑖)
KCL at the three buses
𝐼1 = 𝐼 12 + 𝐼13 = 𝑦 12(𝑉1 − 𝑉2) + 𝑦13(𝑉1 − 𝑉3),
𝐼2 = 𝐼 21 + 𝐼23 = 𝑦 12(𝑉2 − 𝑉1) + 𝑦23(𝑉2 − 𝑉3),
𝐼3 = 𝐼 31 + 𝐼32 = 𝑦 13(𝑉3 − 𝑉1) + 𝑦23(𝑉3 − 𝑉2).
Each sum contains exactly the branches connected to that bus.

∗ ,

∗ ,
−0.90 − j0.30 = 𝑉 3 [𝑦13(𝑉3 − 𝑉1) + 𝑦23(𝑉3 − 𝑉2)]

Each complex equality contains a real and a reactive power balance.
The physical relations hold before any voltage targets or generator schedules are
chosen.
ECE 685 | Power Flow I 22/25

Reference: branch powers
For each branch (𝑖, 𝑘) ∈ {(1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 3)}:
𝑆𝑖𝑘 = 𝑉 𝑖 [𝑦𝑖𝑘(𝑉𝑖 − 𝑉𝑘)]
∗
𝑆𝑘𝑖 = 𝑉 𝑘 [𝑦𝑖𝑘(𝑉𝑘 − 𝑉𝑖)]
∗
Real and reactive components are 𝑃𝑖𝑘 = Re{𝑆𝑖𝑘} and 𝑄𝑖𝑘 = Im{𝑆𝑖𝑘}.
The reference direction at each terminal points into the branch.
Bus power balance sums the terminal powers of the branches connected to that bus.
ECE 685 | Power Flow I 23/25

From a network to physical equations
1 Identify the devices and quantities
Record branch endpoints and parameters, device powers, and bus voltages.
2 Write branch and bus currents
Apply the branch models and sum connected terminal currents using KCL.
3 Write the power relations
Use 𝑆 = 𝑉 𝐼 ∗ at branch terminals and buses. Match each net bus injection to
generation minus load.
Next, collect the voltage coefficients into the bus admittance matrix.
ECE 685 | Power Flow I 24/25

Summary
1 Devices and buses carry voltage, current, and power quantities.
2 Branch models relate terminal currents to endpoint voltages.
3 KCL and complex power give the physical balance equations.
The same relations apply throughout the network. Operating specifications will later
determine which quantities are given and which must be solved.
Build the network relation I = YbusV by collecting the current equations.
